payload.detail: REVIEW 2026-09-25 (offline audit of current main; no provider access): The close condition now has a negative answer: during the 27-hour production deploy stall on 2026-09-21/22, monitor issue #2973 was opened and updated and nobody acted on it. GitHub-issue routing is proven to fire but not to reach a person. Next action: choose a channel that reaches the owner (phone push, Slack or page). Fact fix: live-monitor routing shipped in #2877 (28dabe0c3), not #2884 (which covered CI on main and eval). The stall's own root cause is tracked separately (inbox add of 2026-09-22); CI on main is #T82ND3. PRIOR DETAIL: TWO OF THE THREE SYSTEMS NOW REPORT, as of 2026-09-18. (1) LIVE MONITOR: live-domain-monitor.yml had no failure handling at all — a grep for issue, notify or any conditional step returned nothing, which is why a real catalogue outage went unreported for about eighteen hours. PR #2884 (merged) gave it the eval-canary failure-issue step. (2) SENTRY: PR #2890 (merged) fixed log delivery across Next's bundle split, so application logs actually reach Sentry rather than being dropped at the boundary. (3) CI ON MAIN is tracked as #T82ND3 and also shipped in #2884. WHAT REMAINS: none of the three has been confirmed against a real production failure — all were verified by workflow tests, not by watching one fire. Dedupe was reviewed (label-based find-or-create, so a flake cannot spawn an issue per run) but likewise not observed under load. Close once a genuine outage has produced a notification someone acted on.
